newsitem.title: INDIA: India ICICI reduces prime lending rates.
newsitem.headline: India ICICI reduces prime lending rates.

text.p: The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Ltd (ICICI) said on Tuesday it will reduce its prime lending rates from May 1.
The medium-term prime rate will be 13.5 percent per annum and the long-term rate will be 15 percent per annum, an official said.

"We will have two prime rates from now on," the official said. "There will be a medium-term prime rate for borrowings with a maturity not exceeding 30 months and a long-term rate for borrowings exceeding 30 months."
Earlier ICICI had one prime rate of 16.5 percent per annum.
The spread would remain unchanged at a maximum of 3.5 percentage points over the prime rate, the official said.
ICICI is one of India's leading term lending banks.
"We have decided to reduce the interest rates in view of the current environment," the official said.
"Both the rates will be reviewed and reset periodically as per the prevailing conditions."
"We expect the cost of rupee borrowings to be significantly lower in 1997/98 as compared to the previous year."
The official also said ICICI's loan disbursals grew 16 percent to 111.81 billion rupees in financial year 1996/97 (april-March).
The Reserve Bank of India announced measures to reduce deposit rates in its monetary policy for the first half of financial year 1997/98 (April-March), released on April 15.
Several banks cut their prime rates between 50 and 150 basis points, folloiwng the policy announcement.
On Monday, India's leading term lender, the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) cut its prime lending rate to 15.0 percent per annum from 16.5 percent.
